speaker: Doctor
text:
I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having shooting ear pain and difficulty wearing earrings after a tympanoplasty; can you tell me exactly where the pain is located and if it happens when you chew or swallow?

REQUEST TEST: Otoscopy

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient has a history of polycystic ovarian syndrome, depression, and chronic bilateral ear infections. She underwent right ear tympanoplasty 12 weeks ago. Although audiology report from one week ago showed improved hearing by 20 decibels, she reports occasional shooting pain when eating and discomfort when wearing earrings. She describes her job as stressful and mentions poor sleep quality.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Occasional shooting pain in the ear with eating. I also have Discomfort when wearing earrings, Stress from job, Poor sleep quality. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Tuberculosis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The mention of tuberculosis is concerning given your history of tympanoplasty, but that diagnosis does not typically cause shooting pain specifically triggered by chewing or earrings. Could you clarify if the pain radiates to the jaw or is localized to the surgical site, and do you have any hearing changes or a sensation of fullness?

REQUEST TEST: High-resolution CT Temporal Bone; REQUEST IMAGES: CT_Temporal_Bone.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Chronic Otitis Media with Cholesteatoma or Granulation Tissue Recurrence.

The normal test readings and lack of systemic symptoms like fever or night sweats make the previously suggested Tuberculosis unlikely. Given your history of tympanoplasty, pain with chewing, and sensitivity to earrings, there is a high probability of recurrent cholesteatoma or granulation tissue at the surgical site. Can you describe what the otoscopy revealed, and do you notice any discharge from the ear?
